hook.en: Sound familiar? "She go to school every day." Almost every Vietnamese learner says this — and the fix is one tiny letter.
hook.vi: Nghe quen không? "She go to school every day." Gần như bạn nào học tiếng Anh ban đầu cũng nói y vậy — mà cách sửa chỉ là **một chữ cái thôi**.
hook.ja: 「She go to school every day.」と言っていませんか？日本語も動詞は主語で変化しません。「彼女は行く」も「私は行く」も同じ「行く」。だから英語の **-s** は、日本語話者にとっても盲点です。
hook.id: Pernah dengar? "She go to school every day." Hampir semua pelajar Indonesia mengatakan ini — dan perbaikannya cuma satu huruf kecil.

why.en: In Vietnamese, the verb never changes. "Tôi đi", "cô ấy đi", "chúng tôi đi" — same **đi**. So your ear doesn't expect the verb to move when the subject changes.
why.vi: Tiếng Việt mình động từ không bao giờ đổi. "Tôi đi", "cô ấy đi", "chúng tôi đi" — vẫn là **đi**. Nên tai của bạn không quen với việc động từ phải đổi khi chủ ngữ đổi.
why.ja: 日本語も同じです。「私は行く」「彼女は行く」「みんな行く」— 動詞「行く」は変わりません。でも英語は、主語が **he / she / it** のとき、動詞に **-s** を付けないと不自然に聞こえます。これは日本語にないルールなので、意識しないと絶対に忘れます。
why.id: Dalam bahasa Indonesia, kata kerja tidak pernah berubah. "Saya pergi", "dia pergi", "kami pergi" — tetap **pergi**. Jadi telinga kamu tidak terbiasa dengan kata kerja yang berubah saat subjek berubah.

pattern.en: When the subject is **he**, **she**, or **it** (or anything you could replace with one of those — "my brother", "the train", "Lan"), add **-s** to the verb. "He works." "The train leaves." "Lan watches TV."
pattern.vi: Khi chủ ngữ là **he**, **she**, **it** (hoặc bất cứ từ nào có thể thay bằng một trong ba — "my brother", "the train", "Lan"), thì thêm **-s** vào động từ. "He works." "The train leaves." "Lan watches TV."
pattern.ja: 主語が **he / she / it**（またはそれで言い換えられるもの —「my brother」「the train」「Lan」など）のとき、動詞に **-s** を付けます。「He works.」「The train leaves.」「Lan watches TV.」語尾が **-ch, -sh, -s, -x, -o** の動詞は **-es** を付けます（watch → watches, go → goes）。**子音 + y** は **-ies** に変わります（study → studies）。
pattern.id: Saat subjeknya **he**, **she**, atau **it** (atau apa pun yang bisa diganti dengan salah satunya — "my brother", "the train", "Lan"), tambahkan **-s** ke kata kerja. "He works." "The train leaves." "Lan watches TV."

practice.en: Say each of these out loud before reading the answer — your mouth has to learn the **-s** sound at the end. "My father drives a taxi." "The baby cries a lot." "She doesn't like coffee." Notice negatives use **doesn't**, not **don't**.
practice.vi: Hãy nói thành tiếng từng câu sau trước khi xem đáp án — miệng phải làm quen với âm **-s** ở cuối. "My father drives a taxi." "The baby cries a lot." "She doesn't like coffee." Để ý câu phủ định dùng **doesn't**, không phải **don't**.
practice.ja: 声に出して練習しましょう。語尾の **-s** の音に口を慣らすのがポイントです。「My father drives a taxi.」「The baby cries a lot.」「She doesn't like coffee.」否定文では **don't** ではなく **doesn't** を使います。**doesn't** に **-s** が付いているので、動詞は原形のまま（doesn't like ✅、doesn't likes ❌）。
practice.id: Ucapkan setiap kalimat ini dengan keras sebelum membaca jawabannya — mulut kamu harus belajar bunyi **-s** di akhir. "My father drives a taxi." "The baby cries a lot." "She doesn't like coffee." Perhatikan kalimat negatif menggunakan **doesn't**, bukan **don't**.

takeaway.en: He / she / it → verb gets **-s**. Say it slowly until the **-s** lands naturally.
takeaway.vi: He / she / it → động từ có **-s**. Nói chậm cho đến khi âm **-s** ra tự nhiên.
takeaway.ja: He / she / it → 動詞に **-s**。ゆっくり発音して、語尾の **-s** が自然に出るまで練習しましょう。
takeaway.id: He / she / it → kata kerja dapat **-s**. Ucapkan pelan-pelan sampai bunyi **-s** keluar dengan alami.

title.en: Past tense — change the verb, not just the time
title.vi: Quá khứ — phải đổi động từ, không chỉ đổi thời gian

hook.en: "Yesterday I work late." Sounds fine in Vietnamese logic — "hôm qua" already says past, right? In English that's not enough. The verb has to move too.
hook.vi: "Yesterday I work late." Nghe theo lối tiếng Việt thì hợp lý — đã có "hôm qua" rồi mà, đúng không? Nhưng tiếng Anh chưa đủ. Động từ phải đổi luôn.
hook.ja: 「Yesterday I work late.」— 日本語でも「昨日」があれば過去だと分かりますよね。でも英語は「yesterday」だけでは不十分。動詞そのものを過去形に変えないと、ネイティブには不自然に聞こえます。日本語の「〜ました／〜た」を必ず付ける感覚に近いです。
hook.id: "Yesterday I work late." Kedengarannya masuk akal dalam logika bahasa Indonesia — "kemarin" sudah menunjukkan lampau, kan? Dalam bahasa Inggris itu tidak cukup. Kata kerjanya juga harus berubah.

why.en: Vietnamese signals time with words like **đã**, **hôm qua**, **năm ngoái** — the verb stays the same. English forces the verb itself to carry the past tense, even when a time word is already there.
why.vi: Tiếng Việt mình báo thời gian bằng từ như **đã**, **hôm qua**, **năm ngoái** — động từ vẫn giữ nguyên. Tiếng Anh thì bắt động từ phải tự mang dấu hiệu quá khứ, dù đã có từ chỉ thời gian rồi.
why.ja: 日本語には「〜ました／〜た」という過去形がありますが、英語の過去形はさらに厳格です。日本語では「昨日、遅くまで働く」のように時間詞で示せば通じることもありますが、英語では時間詞があっても動詞は必ず過去形にします。「yesterday」＋「work」の組み合わせは絶対にダメ。「yesterday」＋「worked」が正解です。
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia menandai waktu dengan kata seperti **sudah**, **kemarin**, **tahun lalu** — kata kerjanya tetap sama. Bahasa Inggris memaksa kata kerjanya sendiri yang membawa bentuk lampau, meskipun kata waktu sudah ada.

pattern.en: Regular verbs: add **-ed** (work → worked, call → called). Verbs ending in consonant + **-y**: change to **-ied** (study → studied). Irregular verbs you have to memorize: go → went, eat → ate, see → saw.
pattern.vi: Động từ thường: thêm **-ed** (work → worked, call → called). Phụ âm + **-y**: đổi thành **-ied** (study → studied). Bất quy tắc thì phải học thuộc: go → went, eat → ate, see → saw.
pattern.ja: 規則動詞は **-ed** を付けます（work → worked, call → called）。語尾が **子音 + y** のときは **-ied** に変わります（study → studied）。不規則動詞は暗記が必要です：go → went, eat → ate, see → saw。日本語にも「する→した」「来る→来た」のような不規則変化がありますよね。同じ感覚で覚えましょう。
pattern.id: Kata kerja beraturan: tambahkan **-ed** (work → worked, call → called). Kata kerja berakhiran konsonan + **-y**: ubah menjadi **-ied** (study → studied). Kata kerja tidak beraturan harus dihafal: go → went, eat → ate, see → saw.

practice.en: Try these aloud: "Yesterday I worked late." "She called me last night." "We went to Hanoi last summer." "He studied for three hours." Listen for the **-ed** sound — sometimes it's /t/ (worked), sometimes /d/ (called), sometimes /id/ (visited).
practice.vi: Nói thành tiếng: "Yesterday I worked late." "She called me last night." "We went to Hanoi last summer." "He studied for three hours." Nghe kỹ âm **-ed** — có khi là /t/ (worked), có khi là /d/ (called), có khi là /id/ (visited).
practice.ja: 声に出して練習：「Yesterday I worked late.」「She called me last night.」「We went to Hanoi last summer.」「He studied for three hours.」**-ed** の発音は3種類あります：/t/（worked）、/d/（called）、/ɪd/（visited）。日本語話者は最後の /ɪd/ を忘れがちなので注意。
practice.id: Coba ucapkan dengan keras: "Yesterday I worked late." "She called me last night." "We went to Hanoi last summer." "He studied for three hours." Dengarkan bunyi **-ed** — kadang bunyinya /t/ (worked), kadang /d/ (called), kadang /id/ (visited).

takeaway.en: A time word alone is not enough. If it happened in the past, **change the verb** — every time.
takeaway.vi: Có từ chỉ thời gian thôi chưa đủ. Nếu việc đã xảy ra trong quá khứ, **phải đổi động từ** — mỗi lần đều phải đổi.
takeaway.ja: 時間を表す言葉だけでは不十分。過去のことを言うときは、必ず動詞も過去形に。日本語の「〜ました／〜た」を付けるのと同じ習慣で。
takeaway.id: Kata waktu saja tidak cukup. Kalau kejadiannya di masa lampau, **ubah kata kerjanya** — setiap kali.

question.en: Which negative past sentence is correct?
question.vi: Câu phủ định quá khứ nào đúng?

options: He don't came to the party.
He didn't came to the party.
He didn't come to the party.
He not come to the party.
quiz.correctAnswer: He didn't come to the party.

explanation.en: Past negative uses **didn't** + bare verb: **didn't come**, not **didn't came**.
explanation.vi: Phủ định quá khứ dùng **didn't** + động từ nguyên mẫu: **didn't come**, không phải **didn't came**.
explanation.ja: 過去の否定は **didn't** + 動詞の原形：**didn't come**（**didn't came** ではない）。**didn't** が過去を表すので、動詞は原形のまま。これは日本語話者がよく間違えるポイントです。
explanation.id: Negatif lampau menggunakan **didn't** + kata kerja dasar: **didn't come**, bukan **didn't came**.

hook.en: "She a teacher." "I tired." "They at home." Every Vietnamese learner says these in their first English month. The missing word is tiny — **be** — but English insists on it.
hook.vi: "She a teacher." "I tired." "They at home." Bạn nào học tiếng Anh tháng đầu cũng nói vậy. Từ thiếu rất nhỏ — **be** — mà tiếng Anh thì bắt buộc phải có.
hook.ja: 「She a teacher.」「I tired.」「They at home.」— 日本語話者も初級でよくやってしまうミスです。日本語では「彼女は先生」で文が成立しますが、英語は **be動詞** がないと文として成り立ちません。**am / is / are** は絶対に必要です。
hook.id: "She a teacher." "I tired." "They at home." Setiap pelajar Indonesia mengatakan ini di bulan pertama belajar bahasa Inggris. Kata yang hilang sangat kecil — **be** — tapi bahasa Inggris mewajibkannya.

why.en: Vietnamese says "Cô ấy giáo viên" — no verb in the middle. English doesn't allow that. Between a subject and a description (adjective, noun, place), you need **am**, **is**, or **are**.
why.vi: Tiếng Việt mình nói "Cô ấy giáo viên" — không có động từ ở giữa. Tiếng Anh không cho phép. Giữa chủ ngữ và phần mô tả (tính từ, danh từ, nơi chốn), phải có **am**, **is**, hoặc **are**.
why.ja: 日本語も「彼女は先生」で通じます。しかし英語では、主語と説明（形容詞・名詞・場所）の間に必ず **be動詞** が必要です。日本語の「〜です・〜だ」に近い役割ですが、英語の be動詞はもっと厳格で、省略できません。特に形容詞の前（「I am tired」—「疲れた」は日本語では動詞扱い）は忘れやすいので注意。
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia mengatakan "Dia guru" — tidak ada kata kerja di tengahnya. Bahasa Inggris tidak mengizinkan itu. Di antara subjek dan deskripsi (kata sifat, kata benda, tempat), kamu perlu **am**, **is**, atau **are**.

pattern.en: **I → am**, **you / we / they → are**, **he / she / it → is**. Past forms: **I / he / she / it → was**, **you / we / they → were**. Use them whenever there's no other action verb in the sentence.
pattern.vi: **I → am**, **you / we / they → are**, **he / she / it → is**. Quá khứ: **I / he / she / it → was**, **you / we / they → were**. Dùng khi câu không có động từ chỉ hành động nào khác.
pattern.ja: **I → am**、**you / we / they → are**、**he / she / it → is**。過去形：**I / he / she / it → was**、**you / we / they → were**。文に他の動作動詞がないときは、必ず be動詞を入れます。「She tired.」ではなく「She **is** tired.」です。
pattern.id: **I → am**, **you / we / they → are**, **he / she / it → is**. Bentuk lampau: **I / he / she / it → was**, **you / we / they → were**. Gunakan saat tidak ada kata kerja aksi lain di kalimat.

practice.en: Say each one out loud and feel the **be** sit in the middle of the sentence: "She is a teacher." "I am tired." "They are at home." "He was kind yesterday." "My parents are at work."
practice.vi: Nói thành tiếng và cảm nhận **be** nằm giữa câu: "She is a teacher." "I am tired." "They are at home." "He was kind yesterday." "My parents are at work."
practice.ja: 声に出して、be動詞が文の中心にある感覚をつかみましょう：「She is a teacher.」「I am tired.」「They are at home.」「He was kind yesterday.」「My parents are at work.」日本語の「〜です」よりも be動詞の方が文の中で重みがあります。
practice.id: Ucapkan setiap kalimat dengan keras dan rasakan **be** duduk di tengah kalimat: "She is a teacher." "I am tired." "They are at home." "He was kind yesterday." "My parents are at work."

takeaway.en: If your sentence has no action verb, **be** is the verb. Add it every time.
takeaway.vi: Nếu câu không có động từ chỉ hành động, **be** chính là động từ. Lần nào cũng phải thêm vào.
takeaway.ja: 文に動作動詞がないときは、**be動詞** が主役の動詞です。毎回必ず入れましょう。「彼女は先生」→「She **is** a teacher.」
takeaway.id: Kalau kalimatmu tidak punya kata kerja aksi, **be** adalah kata kerjanya. Tambahkan setiap kali.

title.vi: If I **were** you — giả định cách

hook.en: "If I was you, I would go." Sounds fine, right? Many native speakers say this every day. But in formal English — exams, business emails, academic writing — there is an older, stricter rule: it is "If I **were** you."
hook.vi: "If I was you, I would go." Nghe vẫn được, phải không? Rất nhiều người bản xứ nói như vậy mỗi ngày. Nhưng trong tiếng Anh trang trọng — thi cử, email công việc, văn bản học thuật — có một quy tắc cũ và chặt chẽ hơn: phải là "If I **were** you."
hook.id: "If I was you, I would go." Kedengarannya wajar, kan? Banyak penutur asli mengatakannya setiap hari. Tapi dalam bahasa Inggris formal — ujian, email bisnis, tulisan akademik — ada aturan yang lebih tua dan lebih ketat: "If I **were** you."

why.en: This comes from the English subjunctive mood — a leftover from older English that survives in a few places. After **if** and **wish** in unreal (contrary-to-fact) situations, formal English uses **were** for ALL subjects: *I were*, *he were*, *she were*, *it were* — even though everywhere else you would say *I was*, *he was*.
why.vi: Đây là thức giả định (subjunctive mood) trong tiếng Anh — tàn dư từ tiếng Anh cổ còn sót lại ở vài nơi. Sau **if** và **wish** trong tình huống không có thật, tiếng Anh trang trọng dùng **were** cho TẤT CẢ các chủ ngữ: *I were*, *he were*, *she were*, *it were* — dù bình thường bạn vẫn nói *I was*, *he was*.
why.id: Ini berasal dari subjunctive mood bahasa Inggris — sisa dari bahasa Inggris kuno yang bertahan di beberapa tempat. Setelah **if** dan **wish** dalam situasi tidak nyata (bertentangan dengan fakta), bahasa Inggris formal menggunakan **were** untuk SEMUA subjek: *I were*, *he were*, *she were*, *it were* — meskipun di tempat lain kamu akan mengatakan *I was*, *he was*.

pattern.en: **If + subject + were** → for present unreal situations. "If I were taller, I would play basketball." "If she were here, she would help." "I wish it were Friday." The same rule applies after **wish**: "I wish I were on holiday." The main clause (result) uses **would + verb**: "If I were you, I **would take** the job."
pattern.vi: **If + chủ ngữ + were** → cho tình huống không có thật ở hiện tại. "If I were taller, I would play basketball." "If she were here, she would help." "I wish it were Friday." Quy tắc tương tự sau **wish**: "I wish I were on holiday." Mệnh đề chính (kết quả) dùng **would + động từ**: "If I were you, I **would take** the job."
pattern.id: **If + subjek + were** → untuk situasi tidak nyata saat ini. "If I were taller, I would play basketball." "If she were here, she would help." "I wish it were Friday." Aturan yang sama berlaku setelah **wish**: "I wish I were on holiday." Klausa utama (hasil) menggunakan **would + verb**: "If I were you, I **would take** the job."

practice.en: Try these aloud — your ear needs to get comfortable hearing *were* with singular subjects: "If I were the boss, I would change the policy." "If he were more careful, he would not make so many mistakes." "I wish it were warmer." "If she were in my position, she would understand." In casual speech, *was* is common and accepted. But in IELTS/TOEFL writing and formal exams, *were* is the safer choice.
practice.vi: Hãy nói thành tiếng — tai bạn cần quen với *were* đi cùng chủ ngữ số ít: "If I were the boss, I would change the policy." "If he were more careful, he would not make so many mistakes." "I wish it were warmer." "If she were in my position, she would understand." Khi nói chuyện thường ngày, *was* phổ biến và được chấp nhận. Nhưng trong IELTS/TOEFL writing và thi cử, *were* là lựa chọn an toàn hơn.
practice.id: Coba ucapkan dengan keras — telingamu perlu terbiasa mendengar *were* dengan subjek tunggal: "If I were the boss, I would change the policy." "If he were more careful, he would not make so many mistakes." "I wish it were warmer." "If she were in my position, she would understand." Dalam percakapan santai, *was* umum dan diterima. Tapi dalam tulisan IELTS/TOEFL dan ujian formal, *were* adalah pilihan yang lebih aman.

takeaway.en: After **if / wish** in unreal situations → **were** for EVERY subject. Formal exams care about this — casual speech does not.
takeaway.vi: Sau **if / wish** trong tình huống không có thật → **were** cho MỌI chủ ngữ. Thi cử quan tâm — nói chuyện thường ngày thì không.
takeaway.id: Setelah **if / wish** dalam situasi tidak nyata → **were** untuk SEMUA subjek. Ujian formal peduli dengan ini — percakapan santai tidak.

question.en: Choose the correct formal sentence:
question.vi: Chọn câu trang trọng đúng:

options: If I was you, I would study more.
If I were you, I would study more.
If I am you, I would study more.
If I be you, I would study more.
quiz.correctAnswer: If I were you, I would study more.

explanation.en: Formal English uses **were** after **if** for all subjects in unreal situations.
explanation.vi: Tiếng Anh trang trọng dùng **were** sau **if** cho mọi chủ ngữ trong tình huống không có thật.
explanation.id: Bahasa Inggris formal menggunakan **were** setelah **if** untuk semua subjek dalam situasi tidak nyata.

question.en: Fill in the blank: I wish it ___ Friday.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: I wish it ___ Friday.

explanation.en: After **wish** for an unreal desire, use **were** — even for **it**.
explanation.vi: Sau **wish** cho mong ước không có thật, dùng **were** — kể cả với **it**.
explanation.id: Setelah **wish** untuk keinginan tidak nyata, gunakan **were** — bahkan untuk **it**.

question.en: Which sentence is correct in formal writing?
question.vi: Câu nào đúng trong văn viết trang trọng?

options: If he were taller, he would play.
If he was taller, he would play.
If he is taller, he would play.
If he be taller, he would play.
quiz.correctAnswer: If he were taller, he would play.

explanation.en: **he** still takes **were** in the subjunctive — not **was**, not **is**.
explanation.vi: **he** vẫn dùng **were** trong giả định cách — không phải **was**, không phải **is**.
explanation.id: **he** tetap menggunakan **were** dalam subjunctive — bukan **was**, bukan **is**.

question.en: Fill in the blank: If she ___ here, she would help us.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: If she ___ here, she would help us.

explanation.en: Unreal situation (she is not here) → **were** for **she**.
explanation.vi: Tình huống không có thật (cô ấy không có ở đây) → **were** cho **she**.
explanation.id: Situasi tidak nyata (dia tidak di sini) → **were** untuk **she**.

question.en: Which follows the formal rule correctly?
question.vi: Câu nào tuân theo quy tắc trang trọng đúng?

explanation.en: **wish** + subjunctive → **I were**, not **I was**. Formal, but still used in exams and writing.
explanation.vi: **wish** + giả định cách → **I were**, không phải **I was**. Trang trọng nhưng vẫn dùng trong thi cử và văn viết.
explanation.id: **wish** + subjunctive → **I were**, bukan **I was**. Formal, tapi masih digunakan dalam ujian dan tulisan.

title.en: Inversion — flip the word order for impact
title.vi: Đảo ngữ — đảo trật tự từ để nhấn mạnh
title.id: Inversi — balik urutan kata untuk dampak

hook.en: "Never I have seen such a beautiful view." Sounds almost right to an Indonesian ear — **tidak pernah saya lihat** is natural in Indonesian. But English demands the verb flip: **Never have I seen…**
hook.vi: "Never I have seen such a beautiful view." Nghe gần đúng với tai người Việt — **chưa bao giờ tôi thấy** là tự nhiên trong tiếng Việt. Nhưng tiếng Anh đòi hỏi đảo động từ: **Never have I seen…**
hook.id: "Never I have seen such a beautiful view." Kedengarannya hampir benar di telinga orang Indonesia — **tidak pernah saya lihat** itu wajar dalam bahasa Indonesia. Tapi bahasa Inggris menuntut kata kerjanya dibalik: **Never have I seen…**

why.en: Indonesian often fronts adverbs without changing word order — **Mungkin dia sudah pergi** keeps subject-verb intact. English inverts subject and auxiliary after negative or restrictive adverbials like **never**, **rarely**, **not only**, **hardly**, **no sooner**, **under no circumstances**. The inversion signals emphasis and formality — it's a C2-level feature that separates proficient from native-like writing.
why.vi: Tiếng Việt thường đưa trạng từ lên đầu câu mà không đảo trật tự từ — **Có lẽ anh ấy đã đi rồi** giữ nguyên chủ ngữ-động từ. Tiếng Anh đảo chủ ngữ và trợ động từ sau các trạng từ phủ định hoặc hạn chế như **never**, **rarely**, **not only**, **hardly**, **no sooner**, **under no circumstances**. Đảo ngữ là dấu hiệu nhấn mạnh và trang trọng — đây là kỹ năng cấp C2 phân biệt người thành thạo với người viết như bản ngữ.
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia sering meletakkan kata keterangan di depan tanpa mengubah urutan kata — **Mungkin dia sudah pergi** tetap subjek-kata kerja. Bahasa Inggris membalik subjek dan kata bantu setelah kata keterangan negatif atau restriktif seperti **never**, **rarely**, **not only**, **hardly**, **no sooner**, **under no circumstances**. Inversi menandakan penekanan dan formalitas — ini adalah fitur level C2 yang membedakan penulis mahir dari penulis seperti penutur asli.

pattern.en: Negative/restrictive adverbial + auxiliary + subject + main verb. **Never** + **have** + **I** + seen. **Not only** + **did** + **she** + finish. **Rarely** + **does** + **he** + complain. **No sooner** + **had** + **we** + arrived than… **Under no circumstances** + **should** + **you** + open that door. The auxiliary matches the tense; if there's no auxiliary in the original, add **do/does/did**.
pattern.vi: Trạng từ phủ định/hạn chế + trợ động từ + chủ ngữ + động từ chính. **Never** + **have** + **I** + seen. **Not only** + **did** + **she** + finish. **Rarely** + **does** + **he** + complain. **No sooner** + **had** + **we** + arrived than… **Under no circumstances** + **should** + **you** + open that door. Trợ động từ phải hợp thì; nếu câu gốc không có trợ động từ, thêm **do/does/did**.
pattern.id: Kata keterangan negatif/restriktif + kata bantu + subjek + kata kerja utama. **Never** + **have** + **I** + seen. **Not only** + **did** + **she** + finish. **Rarely** + **does** + **he** + complain. **No sooner** + **had** + **we** + arrived than… **Under no circumstances** + **should** + **you** + open that door. Kata bantu harus sesuai tense; kalau kalimat aslinya tidak punya kata bantu, tambahkan **do/does/did**.

practice.en: Rewrite aloud: "I have never seen such dedication." → "Never have I seen such dedication." "She not only finished early, but she also helped others." → "Not only did she finish early, but she also helped others." "You should open that door under no circumstances." → "Under no circumstances should you open that door." Feel how the inversion puts weight on the first word.
practice.vi: Viết lại thành tiếng: "I have never seen such dedication." → "Never have I seen such dedication." "She not only finished early, but she also helped others." → "Not only did she finish early, but she also helped others." "You should open that door under no circumstances." → "Under no circumstances should you open that door." Cảm nhận cách đảo ngữ đặt trọng lượng vào từ đầu câu.
practice.id: Tulis ulang dengan keras: "I have never seen such dedication." → "Never have I seen such dedication." "She not only finished early, but she also helped others." → "Not only did she finish early, but she also helped others." "You should open that door under no circumstances." → "Under no circumstances should you open that door." Rasakan bagaimana inversi memberi bobot pada kata pertama.

takeaway.en: When a negative or restrictive word opens the sentence, flip the auxiliary and subject. It's the rhythm of formal, confident English.
takeaway.vi: Khi một từ phủ định hoặc hạn chế mở đầu câu, hãy đảo trợ động từ và chủ ngữ. Đó là nhịp điệu của tiếng Anh trang trọng và tự tin.
takeaway.id: Saat kata negatif atau restriktif membuka kalimat, balik kata bantu dan subjek. Itulah ritme bahasa Inggris formal yang percaya diri.

question.en: Choose the correct sentence:
question.vi: Chọn câu đúng:

options: Never I have been so insulted.
Never have I been so insulted.
quiz.correctAnswer: Never have I been so insulted.

explanation.en: **Never** triggers inversion → auxiliary **have** before subject **I**.
explanation.vi: **Never** kích hoạt đảo ngữ → trợ động từ **have** trước chủ ngữ **I**.
explanation.id: **Never** memicu inversi → kata bantu **have** sebelum subjek **I**.

question.en: Fill in the blank: Not only ___ the race, but she broke the record.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: Not only ___ the race, but she broke the record.

explanation.en: **Not only** requires inversion — add **did** before the subject **she**.
explanation.vi: **Not only** đòi hỏi đảo ngữ — thêm **did** trước chủ ngữ **she**.
explanation.id: **Not only** mengharuskan inversi — tambahkan **did** sebelum subjek **she**.

question.en: Fill in the blank: Rarely ___ such dedication in one so young.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: Rarely ___ such dedication in one so young.

explanation.en: **Rarely** at the start → **does** + subject + bare verb. Present simple, so use **does**.
explanation.vi: **Rarely** ở đầu câu → **does** + chủ ngữ + động từ gốc. Thì hiện tại đơn nên dùng **does**.
explanation.id: **Rarely** di awal → **does** + subjek + kata kerja dasar. Present simple, jadi pakai **does**.

question.en: Choose the correct sentence:
question.vi: Chọn câu đúng:

options: Under no circumstances you should lie.
Under no circumstances should you lie.
Under no circumstances do you lie.
quiz.correctAnswer: Under no circumstances should you lie.

explanation.en: **Under no circumstances** requires inversion — the modal **should** flips with the subject **you**.
explanation.vi: **Under no circumstances** đòi hỏi đảo ngữ — modal **should** đảo với chủ ngữ **you**.
explanation.id: **Under no circumstances** mengharuskan inversi — modal **should** dibalik dengan subjek **you**.

question.en: Fill in the blank: No sooner ___ than the rain started.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: No sooner ___ than the rain started.

explanation.en: **No sooner** + past perfect inversion → **had** + subject + past participle. Matches **than**.
explanation.vi: **No sooner** + đảo ngữ quá khứ hoàn thành → **had** + chủ ngữ + V3. Ghép với **than**.
explanation.id: **No sooner** + inversi past perfect → **had** + subjek + past participle. Berpasangan dengan **than**.

title.en: Cleft sentences — put the focus where it counts
title.vi: Câu chẻ — đặt trọng tâm vào đúng chỗ
title.id: Kalimat cleft — letakkan fokus di tempat yang tepat

hook.en: "John broke the window." Fine. But what if you need to clear John's name? "It wasn't John who broke the window." That's a cleft sentence — and it does something Indonesian's **yang** construction can't quite match.
hook.vi: "John broke the window." Ổn. Nhưng nếu bạn cần minh oan cho John thì sao? "It wasn't John who broke the window." Đó là câu chẻ — và nó làm điều mà cấu trúc **chính… là…** trong tiếng Việt không làm được hoàn toàn.
hook.id: "John broke the window." Oke. Tapi gimana kalau kamu perlu membersihkan nama John? "It wasn't John who broke the window." Itu kalimat cleft — dan dia melakukan sesuatu yang konstruksi **yang** dalam bahasa Indonesia tidak bisa sepenuhnya tiru.

why.en: Indonesian uses **yang** to highlight: **Yang memecahkan jendela itu John**. English has a richer system: **It-clefts** (**It was John who broke the window**) pull one element into focus; **Wh-clefts** (**What I need is more time**) package a whole idea as the subject. At C2 level, choosing the right cleft structure lets you control exactly what the reader notices first — and that precision marks advanced, purposeful writing.
why.vi: Tiếng Việt dùng **chính… là…** hoặc **… là người…** để nhấn mạnh: **Chính John là người làm vỡ cửa sổ**. Tiếng Anh có hệ thống phong phú hơn: **It-cleft** (**It was John who broke the window**) kéo một yếu tố vào tiêu điểm; **Wh-cleft** (**What I need is more time**) đóng gói cả một ý thành chủ ngữ. Ở cấp C2, chọn đúng cấu trúc cleft cho phép bạn kiểm soát chính xác điều người đọc chú ý đầu tiên — và sự chính xác đó đánh dấu lối viết nâng cao, có chủ đích.
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia menggunakan **yang** untuk menyoroti: **Yang memecahkan jendela itu John**. Bahasa Inggris punya sistem yang lebih kaya: **It-cleft** (**It was John who broke the window**) menarik satu elemen ke fokus; **Wh-cleft** (**What I need is more time**) mengemas seluruh ide sebagai subjek. Di level C2, memilih struktur cleft yang tepat memungkinkan kamu mengontrol persis apa yang pertama kali pembaca perhatikan — dan presisi itu menandai tulisan mahir yang punya tujuan.

pattern.en: **It-cleft**: **It + be + focused-element + who/that + rest-of-clause**. **It was the noise that woke me.** (focus = the noise). **Wh-cleft** (pseudo-cleft): **What/Where/Why/How + clause + be + focused-element**. **What bothers me is the attitude.** (focus = the attitude). **All-cleft**: **All + clause + be + focused-element**. **All I want is a chance.**
pattern.vi: **It-cleft**: **It + be + yếu-tố-nhấn + who/that + phần-còn-lại**. **It was the noise that woke me.** (nhấn = the noise). **Wh-cleft**: **What/Where/Why/How + mệnh-đề + be + yếu-tố-nhấn**. **What bothers me is the attitude.** (nhấn = the attitude). **All-cleft**: **All + mệnh-đề + be + yếu-tố-nhấn**. **All I want is a chance.**
pattern.id: **It-cleft**: **It + be + elemen-difokuskan + who/that + sisa-klausa**. **It was the noise that woke me.** (fokus = the noise). **Wh-cleft**: **What/Where/Why/How + klausa + be + elemen-difokuskan**. **What bothers me is the attitude.** (fokus = the attitude). **All-cleft**: **All + klausa + be + elemen-difokuskan**. **All I want is a chance.**

practice.en: Transform aloud: "The disrespect made me angry." → "What made me angry was the disrespect." "I just want a fair chance." → "All I want is a fair chance." "The manager, not the team, decided this." → "It was the manager who decided this, not the team." Notice how each version directs the spotlight differently.
practice.vi: Biến đổi thành tiếng: "The disrespect made me angry." → "What made me angry was the disrespect." "I just want a fair chance." → "All I want is a fair chance." "The manager, not the team, decided this." → "It was the manager who decided this, not the team." Để ý cách mỗi phiên bản hướng ánh đèn sân khấu khác nhau.
practice.id: Ubah dengan keras: "The disrespect made me angry." → "What made me angry was the disrespect." "I just want a fair chance." → "All I want is a fair chance." "The manager, not the team, decided this." → "It was the manager who decided this, not the team." Perhatikan bagaimana setiap versi mengarahkan sorotan secara berbeda.

takeaway.en: Cleft sentences aren't decoration — they control attention. At C2, every word you place is a choice about what the reader feels first.
takeaway.vi: Câu chẻ không phải để trang trí — chúng kiểm soát sự chú ý. Ở cấp C2, mỗi từ bạn đặt là một lựa chọn về điều người đọc cảm nhận đầu tiên.
takeaway.id: Kalimat cleft bukan hiasan — mereka mengontrol perhatian. Di level C2, setiap kata yang kamu tempatkan adalah pilihan tentang apa yang pembaca rasakan pertama kali.

question.en: Choose the correct cleft sentence:
question.vi: Chọn câu chẻ đúng:

options: What I need is more time.
What I need it is more time.
That I need is more time.
quiz.correctAnswer: What I need is more time.

explanation.en: **Wh-cleft**: **What** + clause + **is** + focused element. No extra pronoun **it** needed.
explanation.vi: **Wh-cleft**: **What** + mệnh đề + **is** + yếu tố nhấn mạnh. Không cần thêm đại từ **it**.
explanation.id: **Wh-cleft**: **What** + klausa + **is** + elemen yang difokuskan. Tidak perlu kata ganti tambahan **it**.

question.en: Fill in the blank: It ___ the weather that ruined the trip.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: It ___ the weather that ruined the trip.

explanation.en: **It-cleft** uses **be** agreeing with the focused element. **The weather** is singular → **was**.
explanation.vi: **It-cleft** dùng **be** hòa hợp với yếu tố nhấn. **The weather** số ít → **was**.
explanation.id: **It-cleft** menggunakan **be** yang sesuai dengan elemen fokus. **The weather** tunggal → **was**.

question.en: Fill in the blank: ___ bothers me is his attitude, not his words.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: ___ bothers me is his attitude, not his words.

explanation.en: **Wh-cleft** opens with **What** when the focused element is a thing or idea.
explanation.vi: **Wh-cleft** mở đầu bằng **What** khi yếu tố nhấn mạnh là một vật hoặc ý tưởng.
explanation.id: **Wh-cleft** dibuka dengan **What** saat elemen yang difokuskan adalah benda atau ide.

question.en: Choose the correct sentence:
question.vi: Chọn câu đúng:

options: All I want it is a fair chance.
All I want is a fair chance.
All what I want is a fair chance.
All that I want it is a fair chance.
quiz.correctAnswer: All I want is a fair chance.

explanation.en: **All-cleft**: **All** + clause (no **what**) + **be** + element. No extra pronoun.
explanation.vi: **All-cleft**: **All** + mệnh đề (không có **what**) + **be** + yếu tố. Không thêm đại từ thừa.
explanation.id: **All-cleft**: **All** + klausa (tanpa **what**) + **be** + elemen. Tanpa kata ganti tambahan.

question.en: Fill in the blank: It wasn't the noise ___ woke me; it was the light.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: It wasn't the noise ___ woke me; it was the light.

explanation.en: **It-cleft** with a thing → **that** (or **which** in very formal). **Who** is only for people.
explanation.vi: **It-cleft** với đồ vật → **that** (hoặc **which** trong văn rất trang trọng). **Who** chỉ dùng cho người.
explanation.id: **It-cleft** dengan benda → **that** (atau **which** dalam gaya sangat formal). **Who** hanya untuk orang.
